description: Team members with great communication skills and basic coding skills are required.
summary: Wherever we go to fulfill our duties, even if it's outside Earth, we should always prioritize our mental health as much as our physical health. Astronauts are bound to feel isolated, anxious, and lonely in space without their loved ones. To address this, Lunara is developed as an artificial intelligence (AI) based personal mental health companion for astronauts to constantly update their daily mental well-being, get suggestions for improvement, and gain insight by using the provided Lunara chatbot. This is important as it serves as a daily reminder to not only check on one's body but also one's mental well-being or exhaustion level.
details:
What does it do, or how does it work?

LUNARA is a proposed AI-powered mental wellness companion for astronauts. An astronaut checks in daily with mood, stress, energy, and sleep, and can add a private journal entry. They can talk with a supportive AI companion, view personal emotional trends on a dashboard, and use guided meditation, breathing exercises, and ambient soundscapes. LUNARA suggests wellness activities based on how the astronaut says they feel. For example, high stress and low energy lead to a short breathing exercise and a prompt to journal. We have designed the UI/UX in Figma. The AI conversation and offline access are proposed features and are not built yet.

What benefits does it have?

It makes everyday emotional self-care more accessible, personal, and convenient, even when astronauts are far from Earth. It gives them a private space to reflect and simple tools to relax. Over time, it helps them notice their own emotional patterns. It is a wellness companion, not a diagnostic tool. It complements professional support and does not replace psychologists or existing NASA behavioural health services.

What is the intended impact?

We want to encourage emotional self-reflection and make coping activities easier to reach. We want to help astronauts recognise their own emotional patterns, and to support wellbeing during isolation and communication delays. It is meant to sit alongside existing professional astronaut support. We have not tested it with users, so these are intended outcomes and not measured results.

What tools, coding languages, hardware or software did you use?

Used so far: Figma for the UI/UX prototype and user journey.

Proposed, not yet implemented: React Native/Expo for the mobile app, Node.js/Express for the backend, SQLite for local storage, PostgreSQL for the database, and an LLM-based conversational service for the AI. Real deep-space use would need onboard or validated offline AI, because it can’t assume continuous internet.

Hardware: none yet. The concept targets a mobile device.

How is your project creative?

Most wellness apps are designed for life on Earth. LUNARA is designed around astronaut-specific conditions: isolation and confinement, workload stress, sleep disruption, and communication delays. The name combines lunar and aura, and the design is calm, minimal, and space-inspired. It is offline-first and private by default, and it keeps human professional support as a clear pathway.

What factors did your team consider?

Research: we grounded the problem in NASA’s Human Research Program hazards and risks pages, which cover isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, sleep and irregular schedules, and behavioural health.

Offline access: deep-space missions can’t rely on continuous internet.

Privacy: journaling is private by default, with data minimisation, encryption and user-controlled sharing.

AI safety: the AI gives supportive reflection and coping suggestions, with clear limits against medical diagnosis.

Human support: there are clear pathways to mission health professionals.

Honesty about status: we separate what exists (the Figma prototype) from what is proposed, with a four-phase roadmap from prototype to testing and evaluation.
